explanation.text: The Logic: Convexity is defined as the degree of the curve in the relationship between bond prices and bond yields (NISM-Series-X-A, p.169). Because the price-yield relationship is not a straight line, convexity is needed alongside duration to describe how bond prices respond to yield changes. The Trap: A linear price-yield relationship is the assumption behind duration alone; convexity exists precisely because the actual relationship is curved. Note: Convexity describes the shape of the price-yield curve; credit risk and reinvestment risk are separate bond risks measured differently.
